descriptionChirho: A group of people living at the same time; a specific cohort or age-class, often with the article or demonstrative ('this generation,' 'O generation'), referring to the people of a particular era.

Used in the distributive formula 'from generation to generation' (midor ledor / ledor vador), expressing perpetuity or endless duration; Korean 대대로 (daedaero), Arabic min jilin ila jilin, Swahili kizazi hadi kizazi.

Plural construct with possessive suffixes in cultic and legal formulas meaning 'throughout your/their generations' — successive descendants who will inherit an ordinance or covenant; Arabic ajyal, Korean sedaedeul, Swahili vizazi.
Rare sense from the root dur 'to circle, dwell'; a tent-circle or temporary habitation (Isaiah 38:12), supported by Arabic cognate dawr 'circle, turn'.
